description: Run AI Data page — a structured viewer for all data accessible to AI via MCP tools during a workflow run. Organized into grouped sidebar navigation (AI Session, Execution Logs, Captures, Processes, Configuration) with panels for prompts, output, contexts, events, API requests, DOM snapshots, and more.

groups.name: Sidebar Navigation and Data Categories
groups.description: The AI Data page uses a grouped sidebar navigation to organize the many types of data that AI can access during execution. Categories include AI Session (prompt, output, contexts), Execution Logs (events, API requests, MCP calls, image recognition, Playwright tests, AWAS steps, execution spans), Captures (DOM snapshots), Processes (sessions, output), and Configuration (loaded config, dev logs). Users navigate between these categories to inspect exactly what data the AI received and produced, which is essential for understanding AI decision-making and debugging integration issues.

assertions.description: The user can see a sidebar with grouped navigation categories for browsing different types of AI-accessible data, providing organized access to the full spectrum of data that flows between the system and AI
The user can click on any category in the sidebar to load the corresponding data panel in the main content area, switching between different data types without page reloads
The user can expand and collapse sidebar navigation groups to focus on specific areas of interest and reduce visual clutter in the navigation panel

groups.name: AI Session Data Inspection
groups.description: The AI Session group provides access to the prompt that was sent to AI, the consolidated AI output, and the context objects that were available during the session. This is the most commonly inspected data group because it directly shows what the AI was told, what it produced, and what context it had available. Users inspect these to verify prompt quality, understand AI reasoning, and debug cases where AI made unexpected decisions due to missing or incorrect context.

assertions.description: The user can view the exact prompt that was sent to AI for the selected run, including all system instructions and user content, enabling verification that the AI received the correct instructions
The user can view the consolidated AI output for the selected run, rendered with proper formatting, providing a complete record of all AI-generated content
The user can view the context objects that were available to AI during the session, including file contents, configuration data, and other contextual information that informed AI decisions

groups.name: Execution Logs and Events
groups.description: The Execution Logs group provides access to structured event data from the run: task run events, API request logs, MCP tool calls, image recognition results, Playwright test results, AWAS steps, and execution spans. Each data type is displayed as structured JSON or formatted tables. This group is primarily used for debugging integration issues — understanding what API calls were made, what MCP tools were invoked, and how different system components interacted during execution.

assertions.description: The user can view structured event data from the run, displayed as formatted JSON or tables, showing the sequence of events that occurred during execution and their payloads
The user can view API requests made during the run, including URLs, methods, payloads, and responses, which is essential for debugging network-related failures
The user can view MCP tool calls that AI made during execution, showing which tools were invoked, with what arguments, and what results were returned, providing transparency into AI tool usage

groups.name: Captures and Configuration
groups.description: The remaining data categories cover DOM snapshots captured during execution (showing the page structure at specific points), process session data, and configuration information. DOM snapshots are particularly valuable for debugging verification failures — they show exactly what the page looked like from a structural perspective at the time a check was run. Configuration data helps verify that the correct config was loaded during execution.

assertions.description: The user can view DOM snapshots captured during execution, showing the page structure and element tree at specific points in time, which is essential for diagnosing why element-based verifications passed or failed
The user can view the configuration that was loaded during execution, verifying that the correct workflow configuration was used and understanding the parameters that governed execution
Data throughout the page is displayed as properly formatted, syntax-highlighted JSON with expand/collapse capabilities, making it easy to inspect complex nested data structures

groups.name: Pagination and Memory Protection
groups.description: All data-heavy panels (Events, API Requests, MCP Calls, Playwright Results, AWAS Steps, Process Session Output) use backend-driven pagination to prevent webview OOM crashes. Large datasets (240K+ rows, 48MB+) must never be loaded in full. Each panel initially loads a limited page of results and provides a 'Show more' mechanism to load additional pages on demand. The backend enforces LIMIT/OFFSET at the SQL level for unfiltered queries, capping IPC payload size at ~200 items by default.

assertions.description: The Events section loads a limited number of events initially (200 for the events tab, 100 for AI output). When more events exist, a 'Show more' button appears at the bottom with the count of remaining items. Clicking it loads the next page from the backend without freezing the UI. The event count shown in the header reflects the total, not just the loaded count.
assertions.precondition: A completed task run with >200 events is selected and Events section is active

assertions.description: The API Requests section loads the first 50 requests from the backend (SQL LIMIT 50). When more requests exist, a 'Show more' button appears showing the remaining count (e.g., 'Show more (4603 remaining)'). Clicking loads the next 50 from the backend. The summary bar always shows total/success/failed counts from the full dataset, not just the loaded page.
assertions.precondition: A task run with >50 API requests is selected and API Requests section is active

assertions.description: The MCP Calls section loads the first 50 calls from the backend. When more exist, a 'Show more' button appears. The total/success/failed summary always reflects the full dataset. Each call is expandable to show arguments, resolved arguments, response, and error details.
assertions.precondition: A task run with >50 MCP calls is selected and MCP Calls section is active

assertions.description: The Playwright Results section loads the first 50 test results from the backend. When more exist, a 'Show more' button appears. The passed/failed summary reflects total counts from the full dataset.
assertions.precondition: A task run with >50 Playwright results is selected

assertions.description: The AWAS Steps section loads the first 50 steps from the backend. When more exist, a 'Show more' button appears. The success/failed summary reflects total counts.
assertions.precondition: A task run with >50 AWAS steps is selected

assertions.description: The Process Session Output section uses virtualized rendering (react-window) to display log lines. Only visible lines plus a small buffer are rendered in the DOM. The viewer loads 500 lines initially and provides a 'Load more' mechanism when more lines exist. Search filtering and stdout/stderr stream filtering work on the loaded lines.
assertions.precondition: A process session with >500 output lines is expanded

assertions.description: When viewing a task run with thousands of events, API requests, or MCP calls, the webview does not crash with 'Error code: Out of Memory'. The page remains responsive and all sections load their initial page within 2 seconds. WebView2 process memory stays under 500MB even with 10K+ items in the database.
